citations.review_text:
The game is confusing af but I bought it at cheap and it also gave me another free copy which is a huge W.
If you actually wanna play this game just to tell you this game don’t have a good tutorial and you need to find some guides to understand it but overall great game

I know I haven't played much, but first impressions matter, and mine wasn't good.

A friend and I picked up the game during summer sale because of its overwhelmingly positive reviews. At first, things looked promising. The different characters seemed interesting, but the game barely explains what their unique perks and abilities actually do, making it hard to choose one. (At least first time playing. Just pick the default one then, not that big of a deal)

Our first issue came before we even started playing. You can't simply invite your friend through Steam, you have to manually search for the server, which feels unnecessarily outdated. It's a small inconvenience, but it wasn't a great start.

Once we loaded into the world, the game gave us almost no guidance. You're dropped in with little explanation of the mechanics, objectives, or even the basic lore. I understand that some survival games want players to discover things for themselves, but this game often crosses the line between encouraging exploration and simply refusing to explain key mechanics.

The controls also felt awkward. While you can use WASD to move, interacting with objects was REALLY frustrating because my character would often walk somewhere else instead of picking up or using what I clicked on. It made the movement feel very clunky.

The UI is another huge problem. It's one of the most cluttered interfaces I have ever seen in a survival game. It is really annoying to navigate the hotbar, and needing to manually put an item in the equip slot is really annoying. And the worst part is when you change what you have equipped, the previously equipped item is just put in any available slot which gets frustrating when I'm trying to organize something. Not to mention the extremely small icons with names you can barely read. The crafting menu is difficult to navigate since recipes don't clearly communicate what you need or how to obtain missing materials. The "categories" doesn't always makes sense either. …

i bought this game for 1.49 on sale and feel ripped off. it's so disappointing to see that they sell so much full priced dlc for a game which is so clearly not finished to any kind of modern standard for the features it provides.

the game lags way too much to warrant the "difficulty" which is mainly just a bunch of unexplained hazards and obstacles. hosting a server takes more resources than forza horizon 6 on ultra settings, and it's literally just some simple cartoon graphics with no real dynamic systems. it's not fun game design to have no instruction if there are also no environmental or situational cues provided on the developer's part. the end result is just "die to obnoxious hazard, look up solution on wiki" and i think the lack of tutorial is just lazy at that point. 

when i was able to make some progress after some of this frankly obtuse trial and error, i was repeatedly killed by lag spikes that made it impossible to fuel my fire and then caused me to drop all my fuel directly next to the fire instead in pitch black, which i could not pick up despite it literally touching me. i could not craft a new torch or fire because the fuel is the same resource needed to build the thing. this is not difficulty, that's just awful ui and qol even not speaking for the lag spike. 

i get that im getting stronger as i play, but it's simply not fun to lose this often, and it doesnt feel like a roguelite if when i respawn i can literally die on the spot due to it being too dark at the literal spawn zone on relaxed settings. overall, i would spend more time dealing with all of the frustrating and unenjoyable aspects of the game if it were not optimized like literal malware. 7000mb+ to run a server with only myself in it?

i have a feeling that the reason there is no simple "single player" mode to select in this game is because the developers would make no profit whatsoever if they had to carry any of this ridiculously unoptimized overhead.
Good game, but U need to read the wiki or watch a vid to understand the game

Can be a good co-op game with friends / partner / siblings BUT ONLY IF you all like to suffer while gaming. 

I mean like constantly looking for food and to repeatedly die and die and die because of all variety of reasons while slowly understanding how the game works. Cuz the game will not tell you much that is for sure. 
The game was clearly designed to be very difficult and unfair and I have no patience for this. If you do, then go for it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that low-end devices can run the game smoothly at high frame rates and resolutions due to its lightweight 2D and 2.5D art style.

citations.review_text:
Really great game - whilst the learning curve is sharp and rather punishing, it is highly rewarding once you get to grips with the core mechanics. I haven't yet made it far through the progression of the game, but even in the early game a wide variety of options are available, all with their own benefits and drawbacks.

This game is perfect for low-end devices too, as it's 2.5D, hand-drawn art style make it super lightweight. Even on my productivity laptop, I am able to achieve 120+ FPS gameplay at 2K resolution, with no drops or stutters.

The multiplayer system is really easy to use, and allows you to connect with anyone - Steam friend or not - simply by sharing the world's name (provided the world is opened of course). When opening a world, it is easy to choose from private, LAN only, Steam friends, or public, allowing for both solo runs, LAN sessions, or large online worlds.

Overall, a really solid game, and a must play for anyone into survival or roguelike games. I was new to both of these genres picking this game up, and have had an absolute blast with it. I'd say it's an absolute must buy in a sale - and I'd still highly recommend it at its affordable full price.
it can run on a 1gb graphics card , highly recommend for mellow times

I simply don't understand why this game is popular it's outdated even for it's time and the depth is fake! it's all busy work no skill in any aspect just a measure of how much BS you can do until you die

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
This is an acclaimed title among many sandbox survival gamers. However, In my opinion, it leans too heavily on time management and repetitive resource gathering, which becomes exceedingly tiresome. The progression is so obscure that using an external guide is practically mandatory. [b][u]I wholeheartedly do not recommend this title.[/u][/b] 

[h1]It Is Content-Rich[/h1]
[b][u]When browsing its wiki, you'll encounter numerous items and creatures.[/u][/b] Clearly, this game is packed with content, and the developers have poured significant love and effort into it. This aspect alone could be very attractive to veterans of the survival-craft genre.

[h1]Tedious and Obscure Progression[/h1]
[b][u]In practice, you must commit to boring chores just to stay alive: constantly picking and replanting vegetables and flowers to manage hunger and sanity.[/u][/b] Many tools also suffer from very limited durability. This makes the experience dreadfully dull, and exploring the game organically becomes exceptionally difficult when mere survival already consumes roughly 80% of your playtime.

A guide is essential and I truly mean it. [b][u]Newcomers must follow closely to external walkthroughs, treating them like a strict checklist to be checked.[/u][/b] Any improvised goals are effectively prohibited if you wish to make even a little bit of progress.

The mechanics are certainly learnable, but my friend and I are really burnt out for the game. We were unwilling to invest further time and have since moved on to other titles.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3656832240

[h1]Final Verdict[/h1]
[b][u]I have played countless games in this genre, and in my opinion, all of them are superior compared to DST.[/u][/b] While it may be rich in items and mechanics, the overall experience simply is not worth it. With so many excellent games available, and an ever surplus selection to choose from. It seems especially unwise to keep banging my head against this o…

Don't Starve Together is a cooperative survival game that combines exploration, crafting, base building, and unforgiving survival mechanics within a darkly whimsical world. Players must work together to survive hunger, monsters, changing seasons, and countless environmental dangers.

What it does well

✅ Distinctive Art Style

The hand-drawn visuals give the game a unique identity.
The gothic, storybook-inspired world is both charming and unsettling.

✅ Deep Survival Mechanics

Managing hunger, health, and sanity creates constant tension.
Every season introduces new threats that force players to adapt.

✅ Excellent Multiplayer

Cooperation feels meaningful as players specialize in gathering, farming, combat, or crafting.
Surviving difficult situations together creates memorable stories.

✅ Huge Amount of Content

Numerous characters, bosses, biomes, items, and crafting options provide long-term goals.
Frequent updates have expanded the game significantly over the years.
Weaknesses

❌ Difficult for New Players

The game explains very little.
Early deaths are common while learning the mechanics.

❌ Can Be Punishing

Mistakes often have serious consequences.
Harsh seasons and powerful enemies can abruptly end a successful run.

❌ Complex Systems

Crafting recipes, boss encounters, and advanced strategies require time to learn.
Who will enjoy it?

You'll probably enjoy it if you like:

Survival games
Cooperative gameplay
Crafting and base building
Exploration
Challenging progression
Dark fantasy settings
Standout Features
Unique sanity system
Large roster of playable characters
Seasonal survival mechanics
Extensive crafting system
Cooperative multiplayer
Frequent content updates
Verdict

citations.review_text: Great game for when you're bored, alone enjoyable alone but a bit harder than if you played with friends <3

Every time I open my Steam library and see the game, I ask myself: I loved the single-player one, so why didn't I keep playing?

Then I remember.

The single-player experience is already brutal, but DST is on a whole other level when you're alone. It's pretty much not designed for you to succeed.

Regarding public servers, maybe it's my connection, maybe the game is too niche, or maybe it's the netcode. Either way, finding a server with a good connection is a pain. And when you finally do find one...

80% of servers are 80 days in, with everyone running a well-oiled machine. You spawn, die because there are no berries or wood nearby, beg someone for an escort, and have no idea what anything in their giant base does. You genuinely feel like a pimple on someone else's face.

The other option is a fresh server. It's fun for a couple of hours, then everyone leaves and you're left wondering what the hell you're supposed to do now.

I'm sure the game is great when you have friends to play with, hence the thumbs up. But if you don't, you should probably stick to the single-player Don't Starve.
its called together but you can play it singleplayer with a menu pause wich is great if your internet conection is unstable or not fast enough and is fun playing alone to or LAN

Don’t Starve Together is technically built for co-op, but somehow I still lost hours playing it by myself.

There is something weirdly addictive about being dropped into the wilderness with nothing, then slowly running around collecting resources, crafting tools, building a base, and trying not to die because you made one terrible decision at sunset.

The art style is such a big part of the charm. It is creepy, cute, strange, and a little storybook-nightmare in the best way. Everything feels slightly hostile, even when it looks adorable. You are not just surviving nature. You are surviving nature if nature had a sketchy little grin and absolutely wanted you humbled.

I liked the loop of gathering, building, exploring, and slowly figuring things out. Even solo, it was easy to sink into. One minute I was just collecting sticks and grass, and the next minute I had a whole little setup going and was suddenly emotionally attached to not losing it.

It can be punishing, and the game absolutely does not care if you are having a peaceful time. Hunger, darkness, monsters, weather, sanity, bad planning, all of it can ruin your life very quickly.

But that is also what makes it fun.

Don’t Starve Together is charming, stressful, weird, and surprisingly easy to lose hours in, even without anyone else there to help cause problems.

Sometimes the best co-op game is still just me, alone in the woods, building stuff and pretending I know what I am doing.

citations.review_text: If you love suffering, play this game without server/client mods

I WISH I could love this game, but I'm just too stupid for it! That doesn't mean it's not amazing, though! I highly recommend it, especially for anyone who loves the survival genre. It's tough, but it's not exclusionary: you can choose various difficulties, and there are tons of mods in the Workshop. 

Thanks, Klei, for such an awesome Halloween-y experience, even if it's not my type of game! I enjoyed what I got to play.
good game, great fun for co-op, will advise to have the game wiki open in another tab though, mods increase fun exponentially

Fun game. I am a purest when it comes to mods, and in my opinion a game typically isn't worth playing if mods improve it substantially, this is one of those games that I make an exception for (the only other being Space Engineers). 

You're likely going to feel an urge to google something every 2 minutes for the first 3 or so hours, so I recommend a few mods to reduce the urge to do that. Armor values and health bars are a must for me, and provide a confidence boost for what can be an otherwise discouraging take on combat outcomes (there is no way of knowing how weapons and armor compare to each other as far as i can tell). I think a lot of the people with major play time in this game assume you will use mods.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game lacks in-game tutorials or guidance for new players, requiring them to use external resources like wikis and YouTube videos to learn mechanics and craft systems.

citations.review_text:
Most unique survival game of all time. No game by another development team will ever manage to recreate the magic that this game has. I've gone through multiple playthroughs with differing goals and had a blast every single time.

A couple years ago it was a surprisingly complex game due to the lack of tutorials and general knowledge from the playerbase. As a new player, you are thrown into this wilderness without any help from the game. Nowadays there are a lot of youtube videos showcasing farms and mechanics. The developers are also adding skill trees to make the game more approachable which is an overall positive.

Klei have seriously put passion into this game for the past 10 years and it shows. Countless updates that add an expansion or new faction for us to tinker with. The gameplay itself is indescribable and I recommend just playing it for yourself to find out if you like it.

So long as you don't spoil everything for yourself with the wiki, this game has basically unlimited content despite having zero grinding. Learning how to exploit every resource in the world is the intended way to have fun.

Despite that, some clint mods like minimap, persistent compass, announcements, item info, persistent stats, and crockpot prediction will be VERY useful and I do recommend them all.

This game is honestly so brilliantly designed! though for me using the wiki and looking up guides was kind of needed since it has so mutch niche stuff to learn that would be near impossible to figure out,other than that this game has sutch a good gameplay loop,amazing art stile,an addictin farming system and diverse characters.
please buy if youre looking for a good survival game to play with friends.

The original Don't Starve was a fairly tight survival experience and a joy to explore. It's Rogue inspiration could at time makes the permadeath demoralising, though its more contained nature made it fairly easy to drop back in for another go, and the victory conditions present made the game feel cohesive; it had a start, middle and end.

Unfortunately, the multiplayer version of this game has become monstrously complicated and fairly bloated as a result of constant updates. Character revamps and system revamps are frequently implemented, often revamping characters or systems which had already previously been revamped. Revamp! Certainly the game is well cared for and you can most likely look forward to years more updates, though you'll probably need a wiki to even begin to understand what to do.

I wandered off by myself and [b]Starved Alone[/b]... Multiple times! And I also burned my friends camp by accident. And when I say "friends", I mean "random people in the lobby I joined".
This game is hard, it's complex, but it's honestly a good adaptation of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/219740/Dont_Starve/]Don't Starve[/url] to multiplayer.
Surviving is a hell of a challenge, and there are so many mechanics to learn. You can also costumize your character, and collect skins for items. And the artstyle is great, of course.
It's one of those games that are good, but I'm just too bad at it to truly enjoy it.
I just hung out with random people in open worlds, burned stuff (on accident, I promise) and died because I went exploring by myself, got lost and couldn't find food :)
Would [b]Starve Alone[/b] in [b]Don't Starve Together[/b] again!

Really unique survival game, the hand-drawn art style is fantastic and the crafting/building systems have a lot of depth once you get into them. Co-op with friends adds a whole different layer of fun to exploring the world. Definitely worth checking out. Recommended.

A try-to-survive-the-night, barely-make-it-through, die-by-morning, rinse-and-repeat survival simulator.

Played with a bunch of friends, and the number of times we died and had to restart the run is beyond what words can describe. The learning curve, inventory management, and multitasking required are extremely steep, but this never ruins the experience. You’re constantly juggling hunger, sanity, and health while trying to figure out how to survive just one more night. One moment you’re confidently setting up a campfire, and the next you’re being chased by something you absolutely were not prepared for.

Visually, its iconic Tim Burton-inspired art style stands out immediately, while the sound design masterfully makes the world feel both hauntingly eerie and strangely alive at the same time.
